name: Schillaci Underwater Drone
description: Simple printed mechanical construction kit around a purchased 4-inch watertight tube.
scope: 10 checked original STL fabrication definitions. Eight other original STL files fail closed/valid-solid checks and are excluded, including the main thruster and posterior clamps. This mechanical source subset requires source repair and control integration before it can become a complete build.
requirements: Authors recommend solid infill. Match Turnigy Aerodrive DST-700/DST-1200 motor interfaces; BlueRobotics M100/M200 do not fit.
Authors report shallow-water functional prototype dives; no operating-depth qualification is established here.
Choose the thruster configuration and integrate the complete control, power, camera and tether system. There is no complete matched vehicle BOM or firmware in this repository.
purchased: 4-inch BlueRobotics watertight enclosure, end caps, seals and penetrators
Turnigy DST-compatible motors, ESCs, stainless fasteners and ballast
Controller, camera, power system and tether

name: MUR — Miniature Underwater Robot
description: Modular underwater robot with printable internals, hardware BOM, assembly videos, firmware and ROS.
scope: 14 checked original printable STL definitions. One open battery-ring STL is excluded. The full SolidWorks assembly, electronics, complete vehicle BOM and vendor cap remain upstream.
requirements: Match the source BOM and assembly videos. Custom boards and their firmware add substantial integration work.
STL files remain faceted source models; native SolidWorks parts are available upstream.
The piezo transducer and BlueRobotics end-cap STEP are purchasing references; the fabrication catalog does not relicense them as printable or machinable designs.
purchased: Watertight tube, dome/end caps, O-rings and cable penetrators
Thrusters, ESCs, batteries, computer, cameras and sensors
Custom PCBs per upstream production files and electronics BOM

name: FinsROV
description: Eight-thruster ROV with an author STEP assembly, five aluminium CNC details and a printable sensor mount.
scope: Original Configuration.STEP for assembly inspection plus six original fabrication STEP files. The configuration CAD is not a complete verified electrical or procurement BOM.
requirements: Use the original CNC_Maching.xlsx: aluminium alloy, anodized finish and source drill/tap operations. Turning rotational blanks still requires milling/drilling finishing.
Retain O-ring grooves, sealing lands and thread geometry; establish material grade, fits, tolerances and leak/pressure tests for the actual build.
Repository LICENSE is MIT; lower-level controller has a separate GPL license. The README also carries a CC BY-SA badge with unclear scope; preserve upstream notices.
purchased: Pressure cabin and hemispherical dome matched to the source
Eight thrusters, four waterproof servos and four depth sensors
C-board, expansion boards, penetrators, power system and serial tether adapters

name: LoCO AUV 1.0
description: Related open AUV with documented tether control, printed structures and original laser-cut MDF bases.
scope: 19 checked STL definitions and two unchanged original laser-cut DXF bases. Four mounts have unresolved STL units and the TBar fails source/solid volume agreement; those five files are excluded. Remaining files include alternative configurations and are not one matched vehicle BOM.
requirements: Use 1/4-inch (6.35 mm) MDF for the original dry internal bases; upstream requires about a 2-foot laser bed. Confirm drawing units and actual kerf with a test coupon.
The current wiki describes newer skeletonized and all-printed alternatives. Select a consistent design revision instead of combining every source file.
The laser only cuts the original flat profile; drill, chamfer and counterbore as documented. Do not laser-cut PVC or put MDF outside the watertight compartments.
LoCO is an AUV with a documented tether-control option and a more complex computer/flight-controller stack than the simple Schillaci kit.
purchased: Two watertight enclosures with tubes, seals and penetrators
Thrusters, Pixhawk, Raspberry Pi/Jetson and cameras per selected revision
Power system, tether hardware and stainless fasteners
